newsitem.title: GHANA: Ghana's Rawlings near historic poll win.
newsitem.headline: Ghana's Rawlings near historic poll win.

text.p: President Jerry Rawlings looked assured on Tuesday of a historic win in Ghana's elections after dominating the West African nation's political scene for almost two decades.
No incumbent has been re-elected since Ghana won independence from Britain in 1957.
With results in from 179 of the 200 constituencies in Saturday's presidential and parliamentary elections, Rawlings enjoyed a comfortable lead with 56 percent of votes.
His main rival, John Kufuor of the opposition's Great Alliance, had 41 percent, according to the results from the National Election Commission.
If anything Rawlings's lead looks more likely to widen. Of about 20 constituencies still to be counted, seven are from his stronghold Volta Region.
In the parliamentary ballot, the president's National Democratic Congress party had 117 seats in the 200-seat assembly. The combined opposition had 62 seats.

Proclamation of final results - due on Tuesday - is not now expected before Wednesday evening because of the need to double-check some returns from the interior, Election Commission chairman Kwadwo Afari-Gyan told Reuters.
The opposition's Kufuor told reporters on Tuesday: "This is still a tense time and we need to show our strength and maturity so that the country has a chance to move into the future in unity.
"What complaints we have lodged have not been radical enough to reject the final outcome," he said.

With passions running high, an election commissioner said a mob jostled him near the opposition stronghold of Kumasi, capital of the pre-colonial Ashanti empire, after seeing him with a ruling party parliamentary candidate.
Kufuor, 58, said his supporters had been molested in five towns outside Accra. Local newspapers said the army had deployed in the northern town of Sunyani to prevent violence.
Rawlings, 49, a charismatic former air force pilot, twice seized power in the West African nation. He ruled unchallenged for 15 years before first winning a popular mandate in 1992.
Since independence from Britain, all Ghana's elected governments -- except that of Rawlings -- have been toppled before serving out their terms.
The election commission put turnout at about 80 percent.

Commonwealth and Organisation of African Unity observers have paid tribute to the conduct and fairness of the elections. "This is by far the best organised election I have seen in West Africa," one Western monitor said.
Despite tension and some violence in the run-up to voting, polling day itself passed off smoothly.
Rawlings seized power as an air force flight-lieutenant in 1979, executing three former heads of state. He restored civilian rule but seized power again in 1981.
A former socialist firebrand, he embraced Western-style free-market economics, winning plaudits from the International Monetary Fund and World Bank.
